title: UnifyPay rapid evaluation sprint — alignment brief and success criteria
body:
Purpose:
This doc is intended to align Redwood Solutions and UnifyPay engineering on a focused 3-week evaluation sprint ("Rapid Sprint") to demonstrate integration feasibility, measure throughput/latency economics, and validate UX acceptance criteria for a payment-chat augmentation feature.

Context / Problem statement:
UnifyPay wants an assistant layer that helps customer support reps summarize payment disputes, propose next-step actions (refund, dispute escalation, request docs), and surface relevant transaction metadata. They need a short evaluation that proves:
- Redwood can meet the 95th percentile latency SLO under realistic traffic
- Output accuracy and hallucination rates are within acceptable bounds for a payments context
- Integration effort (API + webhooks) fits within UnifyPay’s sprint cadence

Primary goals for the Rapid Sprint (must-haves):
1) Integration: end-to-end prototype where UnifyPay frontend sends a conversation + transaction id and receives a structured assistant response (action, confidence, rationale) via Redwood hosted API.
2) Latency/Throughput: achieve median token latency < 90ms and 95th percentile token latency < 200ms for typical 32-token responses under a 4-instance test harness.
3) Safety/Accuracy: measured F1 > 0.85 on 60 evaluation prompts (dispute summaries) and hallucination rate < 4% (per our internal definition).
4) Ops: run 2 load-test scenarios (cold-start and steady-state) and collect metrics into the Console dashboard (token cost, P50/P95 latency, error rates).

Success criteria (acceptance tests - pass/fail style):
- Integration smoke test: frontend -> Redwood API -> Stable response with schema v1.0 (fields: action:string, confidence:float, summary:string, references:list) (manual).
- Performance: P50 token latency < 90ms and P95 < 200ms across 10k simulated requests with realistic sequence length mix (automated).
- Quality: human-evaluated correctness >= 85% across the curated eval set (random 60 samples), with at most 2 critical safety failures.
- Cost sensitivity: average token cost per session < $0.015 (tracked by Console).

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
In-scope:
- Prototype hosted on Redwood Hosted API (no Dedicated onboarding).
- Integrate with UnifyPay staging environment and synthetic transactions dataset.
- Build ~10 standard instruction prompts and 60 evaluation prompts.
Out-of-scope:
- Full on-prem deployment, production hardening, payments compliance certification.
- Deep UI work beyond a simple embed iframe or API demo page.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Redwood Solutions (Aisha Patel lead): sprint coordination, Redwood API config, monitoring dashboard setup, eval harness and reporting.
- UnifyPay Eng (Luis Romero lead): provide staging webhook endpoints, synthetic transaction dataset, frontend demo integration.
- Applied ML (Priya Nair): prompt design, eval rubric, failure analysis.
- SRE/Infra (Tom Nguyen): load-test orchestration and capacity guidance.

High-level timeline (3-week sprint):
Week 0 (prep, days -7 to 0): data handoff, access, security checklist, confirm API keys and CORS policy.
Week 1 (days 1–7): basic integration, sample prompts, initial model variant tests (base vs quantized). Demo at EOW.
Week 2 (days 8–14): create eval set, run quality checks, iterate prompts, implement structured schema. Halfway review.
Week 3 (days 15–21): load testing, dashboarding, run acceptance tests, compile report and handoff notes. Final review and Go/NoGo.

Workshop agenda (Day 1, 90 minutes):
- 0–10: Introductions, success metric alignment (owner: Aisha)
- 10–30: UnifyPay product walkthrough (Luis) — support flow and transaction model
- 30–55: Data & security kickoff — dataset schema, PII handling (UnifyPay + Redwood security)
- 55–75: Integration plan — API contract, sample payloads, webhook semantics (Tom + Aisha)
- 75–90: Q&A, immediate blockers, and next actions (capture owners)

Integration checklist (tech quick wins):
- Provide sample transaction JSON (fields: txn_id, user_id, amount, status, raw_notes).
- Define API payload contract: conversation_history (list<string>), transaction_id (string), customer_context (map optional).
- Redwood required: API key (staging), allowed origins, max tokens per response = 256, model alias to use: redwood-v1-moderate or redwood-v1-cost-quantized (decided in Week 1).
- Webhook callback for final action, with acknowledgement semantics for idempotency.

Monitoring & instrumentation:
- Metrics to collect: token_count_per_session, p50/p95_latency_tokens, api_error_rate, hallucination_flag_rate (via eval), cost_per_session.
- Dashboard: set up per-route view in Redwood Console and create shared Grafana snapshot for UnifyPay.

Risk register and mitigations (top 5):
1) Latency spikes under warmup — mitigation: increase warmup batching, enable KV cache prefixing for common prompts.
2) Sensitive data leakage — mitigation: redact fields in-transit, use response review gate on high-risk categories.
3) Integration mismatch on schema — mitigation: agreed JSON schema in repo and a small contract test suite.
4) Unexpected cost during load tests — mitigation: throttling policy, token caps per session.
5) Evaluation bias due to synthetic dataset — mitigation: mix of synthetic + 20% real anonymized samples from UnifyPay.

Deliverables (by end of sprint):
- Working demo integration (staging), API contract doc, Console dashboard link, evaluation report (metrics + sample failures), handoff runbook (runbook.md).

Open questions (to resolve Day 1):
- Can UnifyPay share 20 live anonymized disputes for eval? (owner: Luis)
- Which model variant should be the default for UnifyPay’s token budget? (owner: Priya)
- Is there an internal legal constraint about storing transaction notes in Redwood logs? (owner: Aisha + UnifyPay legal)

Immediate next steps (48 hours):
- Schedule Day 1 workshop (Aisha).
- UnifyPay to share sample transaction schema and staging endpoints (Luis).
- Redwood to provision staging API key and Console route (Aisha + Tom).

Notes to self / internal reminders:
- Keep quantized model as fallback if cost/latency tradeoff favors it; record PPL and hallucination delta.
- Build short eval rubric with severity tags: info, minor, major, critical.
- Add a template for action confirmation (user-visible) to avoid automated refund mistakes.

Appendix (sample eval prompt examples):
1) 'Customer claims double charge for order #1234 — summarize dispute and recommend next step.'
2) 'User uploaded invoice with mismatched total — what are action options and confidence?'
3) 'Conversation: agent asks for proof of purchase; customer sends screenshot. Provide a concise summary and whether to escalate.'

End of doc — comments welcome.
